gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Anker's US page says to wall-charge the SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 only with the standard Anker SOLIX AC charging cable, warning that third-party cables may cause damage. The same page rates the AC input at '120V~ 12A Max' while advertising 1,600 W UltraFast, which works out to about 13.3 A at 120 V.
standout_why: Compared against our current page and the rival pages ChatGPT cited that I could open. Our page has the app, temperature and 15 A circuit conditions but no cable rule, no input-current rating and no firmware or extra-battery conditions. Off-Grid Field Guide states no input voltage, circuit amps, firmware or extra-battery effect for any model, and gives the original C1000's 58 min rather than the Gen 2. Amphourly (cited in three chats) has the Anker app rule ('has to be enabled in the app') and says DJI's 100–120 V model is 'listed at 20A max AC current', but has no cable rule, no input-current rating for Anker and no firmware or extra-battery conditions. I could not open thisWATT, Tested Watts or Unplugged Watts (SSL certificate error), so I can't rule out that they mention the cable.
decides: It confirms the Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2 as the pick and adds two conditions to the 49-minute claim: (1) use the supplied Anker SOLIX AC cable, not a spare cord; (2) the maker's own input rating is 12 A at 120 V, yet UltraFast at 1,600 W draws about 13.3 A. Either way, a US shopper needs the station on a 15 A outlet with nothing heavy sharing the circuit. This doesn't change the ranking.

findings.label: Cable required for wall charging
findings.value: Standard Anker SOLIX AC charging cable; the page says 'incompatible third-party cables may cause damage'
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen2 - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Quoted from the page's note under the 49-minute claim, alongside 'UltraFast Recharging must be activated via the Anker app.'

findings.label: AC charging input rating (US)
findings.value: 120 V~, 12 A max, 60 Hz; 1,200 W max standard charging; 1,600 W UltraFast; 1,800 W max bypass
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen2 - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: Arithmetic: 1,600 W ÷ 120 V ≈ 13.3 A, which is more than the 12 A the page lists. 1,200 W ÷ 120 V = 10 A. The figures are as published, and I did not resolve the mismatch.

findings.label: Full charge claim and its condition
findings.value: 0–100 % in 49 min at 1,600 W max AC input, only with UltraFast activated in the Anker app
findings.source_title: Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen2 - Anker SOLIX US
findings.note: The page lists a 32–104 °F charging range. It gives no firmware or outlet requirement. The 68 °F UltraFast threshold is not on this page; our current page sources it to Anker's FAQ.

unsourced: DJI Power 1000 V2 US AC input rating (V/A/W) and fast-mode conditions: dji.com spec and FAQ pages redirect to a 404, store.dji.com redirects to a login page, and the device.report manual returned 403. Amphourly says the 100–120 V model is 'listed at 20A max AC current', which would matter on a 15 A outlet, but I couldn't confirm it on a DJI document.
